promptLatex: From a point $P$ outside a circle, one secant meets the circle first at $A$ and then at $B$, with $PA = 4$ and $PB = 20$. A second secant from the same point meets the circle first at $C$, with $PC = 5$. What is $CD$, the length of the chord cut off by the second secant, in units?
hintLatex: Every secant drawn from one external point reproduces the same product.
Pair each outside length with the whole length of its own secant.
solutionLatex:
Let the second secant reach the circle again at $D$, so $PD$ is the whole length of that secant and $CD$ is its inside piece.

Two secants from the same external point give equal products of outside part and whole length, so $PA \cdot PB = PC \cdot PD$.

Substituting, $4 \cdot 20 = 5 \cdot PD$, which gives $PD = 16$. The inside piece is what is left of that whole length once the outside part $PC = 5$ is removed, so $CD = 16 - 5 = 11$.
